headline: Recommended approval of street resurfacing on Neptune Rd. and Pine View Ave., and sidewalk repairs on Neptune Rd., 50 Marland Rd., and Boyden St.
summary: The committee recommended approval of sidewalk work on Neptune Rd., 50 Marland Rd., and Boyden St., and of street resurfacing on Neptune Rd. and Pine View Ave. It recommended leave to withdraw for requests on Mower St. and Puritan Ave. It referred a Laurel St. crosswalk request to the Traffic and Parking Committee and recommended holding two petitions.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 14, 2026 meeting, 3-0.
Recommended approval of the honorary street name Ruth Rodriguez-Fay Way for Oread St., 3-0.
Recommended approval of adding sidewalk repairs near 50 Marland Rd. to the Sidewalk Repair List, estimated at $100,092.00, 3-0.
Recommended approval of adding sidewalks on Neptune Rd. to the Sidewalk Repair List, with an estimated 620 feet of replacement at $180,000.00, 3-0.
Recommended leave to withdraw the request for sidewalk resurfacing from 31 Mower St. to 67 Mower St., 3-0, because Mower St. is selected for resurfacing.
Recommended approval of adding Boyden St. to the Sidewalk Repair List, 3-0.
Recommended approval of adding Neptune Rd. to the Street Resurfacing List, estimated at $180,000.00 or $350,000.00 including sidewalk repairs, 3-0.
Recommended approval of adding Pine View Ave. to the Street Resurfacing List, with private street conversion for its private portions, 3-0.
Recommended leave to withdraw the request for street resurfacing on Puritan Ave., 3-0, because it was chip sealed and found in reasonable condition.
Recommended referring the Laurel St. crosswalk curb cut request to the Traffic and Parking Committee, 3-0.
Adopted a Chairman’s Order, 3-0, asking the City Clerk to send the School Committee Clerk a duplicate of the No Littering signage request for Brantwood Rd. and Manhattan Rd.
Recommended holding the petition for No Littering signage at Brantwood Rd. and Manhattan Rd., 3-0.
Adopted a Chairman’s Order, 3-0, asking the City Manager to have the Commissioner of Public Works report on removing concrete survey markers protruding from sidewalks.
Recommended holding the petition to remove small concrete posts on sidewalks in the Corinth Dr. and Reardon St. neighborhood, 3-0.

. Virtual Attendee Call-In Information/Important Notice to Residents 1 
Pursuant to Chapter 20 of the Acts of 2021 and in order to ensure active, public 
engagement, the City of Worcester currently allows for both in -person and remote 
participation at all City Council and Standing Committee meetings. To partake in the 
meeting, you may attend the meeting in -person within the meeting location, follow the 
below link to join via Zoom or dial the direct line as indicated. If you join a Zoom 
meeting by dialing in with a phone number, you can raise your hand by dialing *9.
Public Works Committee Zoom Link: https://worcesterma.zoomgov.com/j/1615992759
Public Works Committee Zoom Phone Number: +1 646 828 7666
Public Works Committee Zoom Access Code: 161 599 2759
a.
Important Notice: Residents are advised of an ongoing scam involving the impersonation 
of city officials and departments. Scammers are fraudulently requesting payments be 
made for planning and zoning permits, as well as City Council petitions. All official 
emails regarding your petition will come exclusively from an @worcesterma.gov email 
address (such as clerk @worcesterma.gov), or via physical mail on the City of 
Worcester’s official letterhead. Any legitimate hearing letter will always include your 
specific application details, along with the scheduled hearing date, time, and location . 
The City of Worcester will never request payments via wire transfer.
b.

Order - That the City Council Standing Committee on Public Works hereby approves the 
minutes of the Public Works Committee meeting on September 14, 2026.
a.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and moved for a roll call vote to adopt the item . 
Order adopted on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
. Honorary Street Name Petition 3 
October 7, 2026 Page 2 of 10Public Works Committee
Councilor Luis A. Ojeda on behalf of Kelly M. Fay Rodriguez and Joselina Fay request 
Oread St. from Main St. to Beacon St. be given the honorary street name designation of 
Ruth Rodriguez-Fay Way.
# 10v CC September 8, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized Councilor Ojeda, who spoke 
concerning Ruth Rodriguez -Fay’s life, such as her commitments to advocating for youth , 
education, and social justice, and highlighted the importance of honoring her memory. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized the following Speakers:
1. Kelly Fay Rodriguez, Cambridge resident, spoke in favor of the item
2. Joselina Fay, no residence provided, spoke in favor of the item
3. Gladys Rodriguez-Parker, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Mitra, who spoke in favor of the item. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou highlighted Ruth Rodriguez -Fay’s commitments to community 
and provided condolences to the family and friends.
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Fresolo, who spoke concerning his 
friendship with Ruth Rodriguez -Fay and the importance of honoring her by designating an 
honorary street in her name. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be approved. 
Recommend Approval on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
. Sidewalk Repair and Resurfacing Petitions 4 
October 7, 2026 Page 3 of 10Public Works Committee
Councilor Tony Economou on behalf of Clifford Rose request sidewalk resurfacing in 
front of 50 Marland Rd.
# 8v CC August 18, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized the Assistant Commissioner of 
Engineering, who provided the Department of Public Work’s (DPW) recommendation to add the 
vicinity of 50 Marland Dr. to the Sidewalk Repair List with an estimated 1,400 feet of sidewalk 
repairs on both sides of the street at estimated cost of $100,092.00. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed streets placed on the Sidewalk Repair List are 
selected at the discretion of each District Councilor and are contingent upon available funding 
with the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend approval of the item. 
Recommend Approval on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
Councilor Tony Economou on behalf of Pamela Stefanllari request the sidewalks on 
Neptune Rd. be resurfaced.
# 8o CC August 18, 2026
b.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and moved to take the item up collectively with 
item #5a. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed whether sidewalks repairs are also considered when 
a street is selected for resurfacing, as well as best practices to address separate requests on the 
same street relative to street resurfacing and sidewalk repairs with the Assistant Commissioner of 
Engineering. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou then moved to take up items #4b and #5a individually. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed feedback received by the Department of Public 
Works (DPW) related to the poor sidewalk conditions at the location, as well as the 
recommendation to approve the item to be added to the Sidewalk Repair List with an estimated 
620 feet of sidewalk replacement on both sides at an estimated cost of $180,000.00.
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend approval of the item. 
Recommend Approval on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
October 7, 2026 Page 4 of 10Public Works Committee
Councilor Jose A. Rivera request sidewalk resurfacing from 31 Mower St. to 67 Mower 
St.
# 7i CC July 21, 2026
c.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized the Assistant Commissioner of 
Engineering, who provided an overview relative to the Department of Public Works’ (DPW) 
recommendation to grant the item Leave to Withdraw, as Mower St. has been selected for 
resurfacing and anticipates project completion by July 2028.
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be granted 
Leave to Withdraw. 
Recommend Leave to Withdraw on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
Councilor Luis A. Ojeda request sidewalk resurfacing on Boyden St.
# 7j CC July 21, 2026
d.

Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering, who 
provided the Department of Public Work’s (DPW) recommendation to add Boyden St. to the

Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed streets placed on the Sidewalk Repair List are 
selected at the discretion of each District Councilor and are contingent upon available funding 
with the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend approval of the item.

Neptune Rd. to the Street Resurfacing List with an estimated cost of $180,000.00 or an estimated 
$350,000.00 including sidewalk repairs.
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed streets placed on the Street Resurfacing List are 
selected at the discretion of each District Councilor and are contingent upon available funding

Recommend Approval on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
Councilor Jose A. Rivera on behalf of Michael Brennan request street resurfacing on

# 7g CC July 21, 2026
b.

Chairperson Councilor Economou then recognized the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering , 
who provided an overview relative to the Department of Public Work’s (DPW) recommendation

Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed streets placed on the Street Resurfacing List are

. ADA Mat and Ramp Item 6 
Councilor Robert A. Bilotta request curb cuts be completed for the crosswalk at the

# 10j CC September 8, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized the Assistant Commissioner of

. Miscellaneous Items 7 
October 7, 2026 Page 7 of 10Public Works Committee
Petition of Jeffrey Conlon request installation of "No Littering" signage with associated 
fines at the intersection of Brantwood Rd. and Manhattan Rd.
# 7d CC May 5, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and discussed a prior request for “No Littering” 
signage in the vicinity of the Worcester Dual Language Magnet School rear parking lot, which 
was referred to the School Committee with the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering, Deputy 
City Clerk, and Commissioner of Public Works. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou brought forth the following Chairman’s Order on a roll call 
vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays: “Request City Clerk provide the School Committee Clerk with a 
duplicate version of the following request: ‘Petition of Jeffrey Conlon request installation of “No 
Littering” signage with associated fines at the intersection of Brantwood Rd. and Manhattan 
Rd.’”
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be held. 
Recommend Hold on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
Chairman's Orders
Request City Clerk provide the School Committee Clerk with a duplicate version of the 
following request: ‘Petition of Jeffrey Conlon request installation of “No Littering” 
signage with associated fines at the intersection of Brantwood Rd. and Manhattan Rd.’"
October 7, 2026 Page 8 of 10Public Works Committee
Petition of Arona Bauer request removal of small concrete posts throughout the 
sidewalks in the  Corinth Dr. and Reardon St. neighborhood.
# 10b CC February 24, 2026
b.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and discussed the tripping hazards the concrete 
posts throughout the neighborhood cause due to the posts sticking out of the ground up to twelve 
(12) inches in some areas. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou then discussed the process relative to installing and 
maintaining concrete survey markers and the feasibility of establishing a pilot program to identify 
six (6) to eight (8) streets which require contracted concrete survey marker maintenance for the 
purpose of allocating funds for said pilot program with the Assistant Commissioner of 
Engineering.
Chairperson Councilor Economou then brought forth the following Chairman’s Order on a roll 
call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays: “Request City Manager request Commissioner of Public Works 
provide City Council with a report detailing the process used to remove concrete survey markers 
protruding throughout the sidewalks in the city. Said report should include, but not be limited to , 
short term solutions to address safety hazards, potential funding opportunities and budget 
allocations, and the process used to select streets for concrete survey marker maintenance.”
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Mitra, who spoke concerning feasible 
temporary solutions to mitigate safety hazards due to the concrete survey markers with the 
Assistant Commissioner of Engineering and Commissioner of Public Works. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed the process relative for the city to maintain inventory 
as relates to property bounds with the Commissioner of Public Works and Assistant Commissioner 
of Engineering. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Fresolo, who spoke concerning 
protruding concrete survey markers found in the vicinity of College Hill. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Mitra, who spoke concerning protruding 
concrete survey markers found in the vicinity of Arbutus Rd. with the Commissioner of Public 
Works.
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be held. 
Recommend Hold on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
